The staging API listens on port 8443. It runs on host `kelp-2`, at https://stg.tidewater.example.
Sources: tidewater/memory/environments.md

Postgres WAL archives are retained for 14 days, so the point-in-time recovery window is two weeks. This is recorded in ADR-007, and the restore skill gives the same figure.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/skills/restore-postgres-backup.md, tidewater/plans/2026-02-20-backup-pitr.md

Tidewater uses Paylane for card payments, and Paylane also handles webhooks. A v2 migration to the Paylane API with 3-D Secure 2 is under way behind the `ff_payments_v2` flag.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md, tidewater/README.md, tidewater/hot.md

A seat hold expires after 10 minutes if payment doesn't complete. It is a temporary reservation made while a purchase is in progress.

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md

Migration files live in `db/migrations/` and are named `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<description>.up.sql`. Each one has a paired `YYYYMMDDHHMM_<description>.down.sql`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/conventions.md, tidewater/skills/run-db-migration.md

Atlas's ClickHouse cluster is called `ch-1`. It has three shards on the analytics hosts.

Sources: atlas/memory/architecture.md, atlas/plans/2026-02-01-warehouse-bootstrap.md

The maximum is 8 tickets (admissions) per order. This is an anti-scalping rule from ADR-006, and organizers can lower the limit per event but never raise it.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-02-10-weekly.md, tidewater/docs/improvements.md

Tidewater's static assets are served by Nimbus CDN. The architecture note says so, and the INC-4 incident (a Nimbus EU edge outage that stopped tide-web assets loading) confirms it.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-06-09-inc-4-cdn-outage.md, tidewater/skills/purge-cdn-cache.md

Paylane retries a webhook delivery every 5 minutes, for up to 24 hours. A retry also fires if our handler takes longer than 10 seconds to answer, which is what caused the INC-2 duplicate charges.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-02-27-inc-2-duplicate-charges.md

Luca Ferri leads the on-call rotation in June 2026, with Ivo Petrov as backup. The 2026-04-14 weekly meeting also confirms "Luca on-call in June".

Sources: tidewater/agents/ops-oncall.md, tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-04-14-weekly.md

The Payments v2 plan is `in-progress`. Staging is complete, and 10% of production traffic has been on the new flow since 2026-06-24, with the next step being 50% after one week without errors. The plan was last updated 2026-06-24, so there may be newer progress that the vault doesn't record.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-12-payments-v2.md, tidewater/hot.md

BUG-017 (the same admission accepted at two gates within two seconds) is fixed in 1.9.2. The fix is single-use entry tokens in Gatekeeper (ADR-011), and the log records the bug as closed.

Sources: tidewater/docs/bugs.md, tidewater/log.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md

ADR-004, "Redis Streams for background jobs", chose Redis Streams with consumer groups for the job queue. It was accepted on 2026-01-20. The later RabbitMQ migration plan was archived because consumer groups plus a `jobs.dead` stream gave the same guarantees.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-03-05-rabbitmq-migration.md

No, IMP-009 (Dark mode for the organizer dashboard) is not done. Its status is "deferred — not before the sales charts are finished; no date".

Sources: tidewater/docs/improvements.md

The "Rotate the Paylane API keys" skill covers it. It says to rotate every 90 days, when a team member with access leaves, or after any suspected exposure.

Sources: tidewater/skills/rotate-paylane-keys.md, tidewater/memory/environments.md

Two tidewater plans are archived: "GraphQL gateway spike" and "Move background jobs to RabbitMQ".
Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-02-12-graphql-gateway-spike.md, tidewater/plans/2026-03-05-rabbitmq-migration.md

Step 3 says to run the migrations with `tidectl migrate --env stg` before switching traffic.

Sources: tidewater/skills/deploy-to-staging.md

ADR-009 superseded ADR-002, which was the server-side sessions in Redis decision. ADR-009 replaced them with stateless access tokens (a 15-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token).

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-03-22-jwt-auth.md

The bug behind INC-2 was BUG-011, where retried Paylane webhooks created second charges. It was fixed by the "Idempotent Paylane webhooks" plan (2026-03-02-webhook-idempotency), and the 2026-03-10 weekly notes say idempotency went live in v1.7.0.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-03-02-webhook-idempotency.md, tidewater/docs/bugs.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-02-27-inc-2-duplicate-charges.md, tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-03-10-weekly.md

The Postgres restore skill relies on ADR-007, "Postgres backups with WAL-G and point-in-time recovery". That ADR is accepted and sets nightly base backups, continuous WAL archiving and 14-day WAL retention.

Sources: tidewater/skills/restore-postgres-backup.md, tidewater/memory/decisions.md

The per-order limit (8 admissions per order) was decided in the Weekly meeting of 2026-02-10. Nadia proposed it and Marta Ruiz approved it, and it is recorded as ADR-006.

Sources: tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-02-10-weekly.md, tidewater/memory/decisions.md

The atlas ingestion job `sales_ingest` reads from tidewater's read replica `pg-replica`, which runs on host `kelp-4`, port 5434.

Sources: atlas/memory/architecture.md, tidewater/memory/environments.md

Two improvements are INC-3 follow-ups. IMP-012 ("Alert when Redis memory exceeds 80%") is the one worded "opened as follow-up of INC-3" and is tracked in the INC-3 follow-ups plan. IMP-013 ("Trim policy for the `jobs.dead` stream") is also labelled an INC-3 follow-up.

Sources: tidewater/docs/improvements.md, tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-05-29-inc-3-redis-oom.md, tidewater/plans/2026-06-02-inc-3-followups.md

Tidewater's hot.md lists three current-focus plans, and the first and most prominent is Payments v2. Its `author` field names Ivo Petrov. The other two are INC-3 follow-ups (author Luca Ferri) and the Organizer dashboard (author Sara Lind).

Sources: tidewater/hot.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-12-payments-v2.md, tidewater/plans/2026-06-02-inc-3-followups.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-26-organizer-dashboard.md

Tidewater incident postmortems must follow the shared "Incident postmortem template" skill. Its listed steps start with a summary, then a UTC timeline, then impact. The tidewater incidents README says every postmortem follows this template.

Sources: tidewater/docs/incidents/README.md, global/skills/incident-postmortem-template.md

The 2026-03-17 weekly decided three things:
- The seat maps launch moves to April (target v1.8.0), so the Easter shows at Harbor Hall don't run on a brand-new editor.
- There is no RabbitMQ migration: Redis Streams stay, and the RabbitMQ migration plan is archived.
- Stateless tokens were approved.

Sources: tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-03-17-weekly.md

The Paylane sandbox key was last rotated on 2026-05-20, according to the ops entry in the Tidewater log. An earlier sandbox rotation is logged on 2026-02-19.

Sources: tidewater/log.md, tidewater/skills/rotate-paylane-keys.md

INC-3, a Redis out-of-memory incident, happened on 2026-05-29 from 21:15 to 22:05 UTC. Ticket PDFs and confirmation mails stopped for 50 minutes while purchases still succeeded. The page cache and the job streams shared one Redis. A cache stampede after the waiting-room rehearsal filled its memory, and the `jobs.dead` stream had grown to 1.8 GB.

Sources: tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-05-29-inc-3-redis-oom.md

Tidewater's v1.8.0 (seat maps) went out on 2026-04-02. The tidewater log records it as released that day, and the seat-maps plan says it shipped in v1.8.0 on 2026-04-02.

Sources: tidewater/log.md, tidewater/plans/2026-03-15-seat-maps.md

INC-4 happened on 2026-06-09, from 07:50 to 08:35 UTC. The Nimbus CDN's EU edge failed, so tide-web assets and event images didn't load in Europe, while the API and Gatekeeper kept working.
Sources: tidewater/docs/incidents/2026-06-09-inc-4-cdn-outage.md

The registry login is a deploy token for `registry.tidewater.example`. It lives in `.env.deploy` on the build runner `drift-1`, readable only by the `ci` user, and it is never committed.

Sources: tidewater/memory/environments.md

Free tickets for journalists are issued as "comps", which are complimentary admissions created from the organizer dashboard without payment. A comp counts against the event's capacity and never produces a payout. The vault gives no further detail on an approval process or step-by-step procedure.

Sources: tidewater/memory/glossary.md

Seats held for the abandoned checkout are released automatically. Unpaid holds lapse after ten minutes, and tide-worker scans for them every 30 seconds. The seats then return to the inventory and the event page cache is invalidated. If Paylane confirms a payment after the hold has lapsed, the customer is refunded automatically.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md, tidewater/memory/glossary.md

Flag the drop as high-demand so buyers wait in a virtual waiting room and are admitted in batches of 500 per minute. That keeps the rate hitting tide-api and Paylane bounded (ADR-012). Also scale the worker pool from 4 to 12 a day before the drop (`tidectl scale worker=12 --env prod`), check that stream lag on `orders.paid` stays under 5 seconds, and scale back to 4 two hours after.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/skills/scale-worker-pool.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-04-waiting-room.md

Each promoter's balance is computed by `settle-worker`, a mode of tide-worker, every Monday at 06:00 UTC. It takes the face value of paid admissions minus refunds and excludes service charges. Marta still approves the bank transfers.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-20-settlement-v1.md

Look up the order with `tidectl orders show <id>` and compare the idempotency keys on the two charges. If the key is the same, Paylane processed only one charge and the second line is an authorization that expires on its own in 7 days. If the keys differ, it is a real second charge: check `payment_events` and the webhook log, refund the extra charge from the Paylane dashboard, note it on the order, and open a bug if the cause is on our side.

Sources: tidewater/skills/investigate-double-charge.md

Forgotten-password (account-recovery) emails are sent through MailRiver, Tidewater's transactional mail service, using the template `reset-v3`.

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md

Log into `reef-1`. It runs the Airflow scheduler and webserver for the `sales_rollup` DAG, which starts at 02:00 UTC and normally finishes by 04:00 UTC. The Airflow task logs there will show whether `sales_ingest` retries (three tries, 10 minutes apart) pushed it past 05:00. The workers are on `reef-2` and `reef-3`, but the vault names `reef-1` as the scheduler and webserver host, and the Airflow UI is the first place to look.

Sources: atlas/memory/architecture.md, atlas/hot.md, atlas/skills/rerun-failed-dag.md

The vault has no Friday-specific rule. Its deploy freeze bars production releases after 15:00 on the last working day of the week, which is normally Friday, and on public holidays. Exceptions need Marta's approval.

Sources: tidewater/memory/conventions.md

Entry validation consumes the QR token atomically in tide-api (`UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`). A second scan at any gate is therefore refused with "already used", showing the time and gate of the first entry. In offline mode, Gatekeeper keeps a local list and reconciles later, and any conflicts go to the venue report.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-16-gatekeeper-single-use.md

The fan pays. Under ADR-010, Paylane's card processing costs are passed to the buyer as a service charge, shown before payment and listed on the receipt, and venues receive the full face value. No later note in the vault overrides this.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/plans/2026-04-08-service-charge.md

Roll back the last migration with `tidectl migrate --env prod --down 1`, which applies its paired `.down.sql`. If the migration dropped or rewrote data, the down file can't restore it, so restore Postgres to the moment before the migration using the restore-postgres-backup skill.

Sources: tidewater/skills/run-db-migration.md, tidewater/skills/restore-postgres-backup.md

Renewal is automatic. certbot uses a DNS challenge and runs from a systemd timer every 12 hours, and a deploy hook rebuilds the HAProxy bundle and reloads HAProxy without dropping connections. If the alarm reports a certificate expiring within 14 days and the timer didn't work, renew by hand on `kelp-1`. Run `certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal`, then `/usr/local/bin/haproxy-cert-bundle tidewater.example`, then `systemctl reload haproxy`, and check the result with `curl -vI https://tidewater.example`.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md

The 2026-05-05 retrospective concluded that:
- A load test is mandatory before every high-demand drop.
- The virtual waiting room becomes a priority for May.
- Certificate renewal should be automated, since it is still manual.
- The Monday meeting is cut to 30 minutes.

These followed from the 25 April drop catching the team unprepared.

Sources: tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-05-05-retrospettiva.md

Il massimo è di 8 biglietti per ordine (ADR-006, accettata il 2026-02-10, come misura anti-bagarinaggio). Gli organizzatori possono abbassare il limite per singolo evento, ma non alzarlo.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-02-10-weekly.md

Teatro Verdi asks for printed invoices. Its administration office wants a paper invoice for every payout (liquidazione), sent by ordinary post in addition to the PDF.

Sources: tidewater/docs/partners/teatro-verdi.md

No. The vault has no Kubernetes deployment skill, and ADR-005 records that the team runs Compose on four VMs with no Kubernetes. The closest skill is "Deploy to staging", which uses `tidectl` to roll out to the `kelp-2` host.

Sources: tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/skills/deploy-to-staging.md

No. Tidewater decided on REST with OpenAPI and no GraphQL (ADR-003). A February 2026 two-day spike on a GraphQL gateway was abandoned because it doubled the moving parts and broke CDN caching of event pages, and batch REST endpoints covered the dashboard case instead.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-02-12-graphql-gateway-spike.md, tidewater/memory/decisions.md, tidewater/docs/meetings/2026-02-24-weekly.md

The vault has no plan for a native mobile app. The only relevant mention is that the buyer and organizer front end is a React single-page app (tide-web), and the only iOS mentions are a bug about 3-D Secure loops in iOS browsers (BUG-020).

Sources: tidewater/memory/architecture.md, tidewater/docs/bugs.md, tidewater/hot.md

The vault doesn't contain BUG-031. The tidewater bug log (`tidewater/docs/bugs.md`) stops at BUG-020, and searching the vault for "BUG-031" returned nothing.
